priorStories.headline: Australian lawmaker loses leg after vehicle attack
priorStories.body:
Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines was in critical condition after surgery and the amputation of one leg following a deliberate vehicle attack in Wangaratta.

Officials said the vehicle struck Haines, reversed and hit her again before a bystander restrained the driver. Counterterrorism authorities were helping investigate, but police had not established a motive or filed charges.

priorStories.headline: Japan launches mission to sample Mars moon
priorStories.body:
Japan launched its uncrewed Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft aboard an H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center.

The mission is designed to study Mars’s moons, collect at least 10 grams of material from Phobos and return it to Earth in 2031. If successful, it would be the first sample return from the Martian system.

priorStories.headline: Kenyan cult members convicted of 191 murders
priorStories.body:
A Kenyan court convicted preacher Paul Mackenzie and 28 associates of murdering 190 children and one adult in the Shakahola Forest.

The court found that Mackenzie’s followers were ordered to starve themselves and their children, while guards prevented victims from escaping or eating. More than 400 bodies have been recovered during the wider investigation. Sentencing was set for November 6.

priorStories.headline: WFP drops 500,000 people from Gaza aid
priorStories.body:
The U.N. World Food Programme said funding shortages were forcing it to reduce planned monthly food or cash assistance in Gaza from 1.6 million people to 1.1 million.

The reduction leaves about 500,000 people without monthly assistance while roughly two-thirds of Gaza’s population remains acutely food insecure, according to the agency.

priorStories.headline: Houthi attack kills 58 at Yemen camp
priorStories.body:
Three ballistic missiles struck a government security-forces training camp in Yemen’s Shabwa province, killing 58 people and injuring more than 200, according to the provincial governor. Fourteen people remained missing.

The Houthis acknowledged targeting the Al-Alam camp, which they described as Saudi-run.

candidates.summary: CBC News projected that Alberta voters rejected starting the legal process toward a binding referendum on separation from Canada after about one-third of ballots had been counted. The province’s first separation referendum was nonbinding and offered voters a choice between remaining in Canada and initiating that process.
candidates.title: Alberta voters reject separation process in referendum

candidates.summary: A Russian drone struck morning traffic near a shopping center in Chabany on the Kyiv–Odesa highway, setting vehicles on fire and killing three people, according to Ukrainian prosecutors. Four others were wounded, and emergency crews restricted traffic while authorities investigated and verified the preliminary casualty count.
candidates.title: Russian drone strike kills three on Kyiv–Odesa highway
